_: THE WORKS. What each figure ACTUALLY WROTE, and where it can be read.
_why: The whole system rests on a claim it could not check. A figure speaks from a record;
the daily quote is ruled to be a citation into the corpus; witness mode answers from
what a figure SAW; and the posting gate refuses an unsourced quotation because it has
no way to verify a sourced one. Four things depend on a corpus that does not exist.
AND THE COLUMN THAT LOOKED LIKE ONE IS NOT ONE. names.csv has a `Links` column, filled
for all 1,011 rows, and every value is the same shape:
That is a link to a SEARCH BOX. It was generated from the name, it points at no
particular article, and it cites nothing. A column that looks populated and holds
nothing is the Silent Signature wearing a spreadsheet.
_law: A QUOTATION WITHOUT A SOURCE IS A FABRICATION WAITING TO BE SCREENSHOTTED. And a source that cannot be reached is not a source — it is a thing somebody remembers.
_scope: ONLY FIGURES WHO LEFT WRITINGS. The roster holds three kinds and this register covers
1 · LEFT WRITINGS — Caesar, Lincoln, Aurelius, Confucius. Their own words survive,
and for nearly all of them the primary texts are public domain and already
machine-readable. THIS REGISTER IS FOR THESE.
2 · LEFT NOTHING, but a primary source exists ABOUT them — Gilgamesh has the Epic,
Socrates has Plato. The citation is real but it is not theirs. Out of scope.
3 · NEVER EXISTED — Apollo, Isis, Prometheus, Tiamat. Several hundred rows. Out of
scope, and the reason the scope matters: WITNESS MODE ASKS WHAT A FIGURE SAW,
and its rule is to say so where the record is silent. Apollo has no record to

abraham lincoln.note: Enormous surviving record — letters, speeches, telegrams, legal papers. The Collected Works run to eight volumes and are the standard citation.

corpus.title: Letter to Horace Greeley
corpus.note: The paramount-object letter. Quoted constantly and MISquoted almost as often — the sentence about saving the Union is usually cut before its second half.

corpus.title: Letter to Albert G. Hodges
corpus.note: Contains the line about events having controlled him.

corpus.title: Gettysburg Address
corpus.note: Five manuscript versions in his own hand differ from one another. A citation must say WHICH — the Bliss copy is the usual text.

julius caesar._keyNote: THE KEY IS THE ROSTER'S NAME, LOWERCASED — and this entry was authored as "gaius julius caesar" and caught by probe-works in its first run. names.csv says "Julius Caesar". THE TERMINAL DISPLAYS "GAIUS JULIUS CAESAR", which is a fuller name than the roster holds, and that discrepancy is worth chasing on its own: the voice resolver keys on the same lowercased name, so a display name the roster does not carry resolves to nothing and falls to the default voice.
julius caesar.note: Two commentaries survive in his own Latin. The Civil War is his; the eighth book of the Gallic War is Hirtius and must not be quoted as Caesar.

corpus.title: Commentarii de Bello Gallico
corpus.note: Books I-VII are Caesar. BOOK VIII IS AULUS HIRTIUS and is not.

marcus aurelius.note: One work, written to himself and never meant to be read. Every English text is a translation, so a quotation is a translator's sentence as much as his — say which.

corpus.title: Meditations
corpus.note: TRANSLATION MATTERS. Long, Hays and Hard differ enough that a famous line may exist in one and not the others.

confucius.note: HE WROTE NOTHING THAT SURVIVES. The Analects were compiled by disciples after his death, so every 'Confucius said' is a report at one remove. That is worth stating rather than smoothing over — it is exactly the distinction the witness rule exists for.

corpus.title: The Analects (Lunyu)
corpus.note: Compiled by disciples. Attribute as reported speech, never as his pen.

corpus.title: Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium
corpus.note: 124 letters. Cite the letter number — 'Seneca said' is not a citation.

frederick douglass.note: Three autobiographies, written across forty years, and they DISAGREE with each other because he revised what he was willing to say as his safety changed. A citation must name which.

corpus.title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave
What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?

_stillToAuthor: THIS REGISTER IS SIX FIGURES OF A ROSTER OF 1,011, AND IT SAYS SO RATHER THAN
LOOKING FINISHED. The honest next move is not to fill it alphabetically but to cover
THE FIGURES A READER ACTUALLY MEETS — the ones with plates, who appear in the codex
and the terminal. Everyone else can wait until somebody asks.
Every url above is null. That is deliberate and it is not laziness: a link typed from
memory is the fault this file was built to replace.
